clue.text: The sound of one often carried?

definitions.text: The sound of one often carried?

parts.words: The sound of one often carried?
parts.note: the thing often carried is a mobile phone, and the clue asks for the noise it makes when someone calls

explanation.definitionFit: A mobile's alert tune is the sound of a phone that most people carry about with them.

clue.text: Item for salad dressing down

definitions.meaning: a peppery leaf, arugula to Americans
British slang for a severe telling-off

explanation.walkthrough: 'dressing' suggests salad dressing, but 'dressing down' is a scolding.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a peppery salad leaf, and in British slang a stern reprimand.

clue.text: Infamy but not Troy, ie at war

indicators.note: at war suggests conflict and disorder, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Ill fame, though not Troy's, in the war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at war' rearranges NOT TROY IE.
explanation.definitionFit: Being famous for something bad is notoriety, a matching word for disrepute.

clue.text: Sample without second veg commonly

indicators.note: without means a letter is taken away

parts.note: a taster is a small sample

explanation.surface: Sample a vegetable lacking a second, colloquially.
explanation.walkthrough: 'commonly' marks a slang word: potato informally.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally a potato, the everyday vegetable, is called this.

clue.text: Certain position of gear change in Renault

indicators.note: a change in the word alters its letter order

explanation.surface: A gear change in a French car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change in' rearranges RENAULT.
explanation.definitionFit: The gear position where no drive is engaged is called by this name.

clue.text: The film of a lifetime

parts.note: read as praise, 'the film of a lifetime' means an unmissable movie; read literally it is a movie telling the story of someone's life

explanation.definitionFit: A screen biography is literally a film about a person's whole life.

clue.text: Deny Tim in fiddling insurance against loss

indicators.note: fiddling with the words tampers with their letters

explanation.surface: Tim denies fiddling an insurance claim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fiddling' rearranges DENY TIM IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Security against damage or harm, a guarantee of compensation, is indemnity.

clue.text: Suggested when no professional put on an act

indicators.note: no means the following piece is left out

parts.note: proposed means suggested
pro is short for professional

explanation.surface: An amateur actor was proposed for a role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' removes PRO from PROPOSED; 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To pose is to affect an attitude, to pretend.

clue.text: Combine two texts to study — even English?

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study
flat means even or level

explanation.surface: An English scholar studying two texts side by side.
explanation.walkthrough: CON as 'study' is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: To merge two variant readings into one, especially manuscripts, is to conflate them.

clue.text: Rake-off by one ticket racketeer? Stop it!

parts.note: a rake-off is a share of the takings, a cut
one is the Roman numeral I
a tout sells tickets illegally at inflated prices

explanation.surface: A ticket tout takes his share of a scam until someone tells him to stop.
explanation.walkthrough: TOUT is the British word for a ticket scalper.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an informal command to desist, the same as telling someone to quit doing something.

clue.text: Inventor with no pretension making comeback

indicators.note: coming back means the phrase is read from its end to its start

parts.note: 'no side' is an old British expression for an absence of airs or pretension

explanation.surface: An inventor drops his airs and makes a return to public life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making comeback' turns NOSIDE to give the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Edison was the American inventor of the phonograph and a practical light bulb.

clue.text: Squandered, we hear Sad

indicators.note: we hear tells us the word is to be taken by its sound

parts.note: blew means squandered, as in blew the money

explanation.surface: Someone who squandered their fortune is now depressed.
explanation.walkthrough: BLEW and BLUE sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling low or depressed is feeling blue, a colour idiom.

clue.text: Slip-up of the rascal when losing head

indicators.note: losing its head means the word drops its first letter

parts.note: a little terror is a naughty child, a rascal

explanation.surface: A naughty child's blunder when he gets flustered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' takes the T off TERROR; 'of the' and 'when' only link.
explanation.definitionFit: A mistake or lapse is a slip-up, a mistake in other words.

clue.text: Top of building backing to the east in list-one to be looked up to?

definitions.text: one to be looked up to?

indicators.note: the letters built so far go inside the word for a list

parts.note: a roll is a list of names, as in a roll call

indicators.note: backing means the word for the top of a building is turned round

parts.note: a dome is the rounded top of a building
E is the abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: Instructions for an architect's drawing, with the dome on the east side, and someone admirable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' reverses the building's top, the east follows it, and 'in' sets the lot inside the list; the hyphen in 'list-one' hides where the definition starts.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone others admire and imitate is a person they look up to, a good example.

clue.text: Treacherous person breaking law, see

indicators.note: breaking the words smashes their letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A traitor is one who breaks the law, you see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' rearranges the letters of LAW and SEE.
explanation.definitionFit: A sly, untrustworthy person is called by the name of the sneaky small mammal.

clue.text: One collecting discarded items craves eg new, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters may be rearranged

explanation.surface: A bin-raider who longs for, say, new things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges CRAVES EG with N.
explanation.definitionFit: A person or animal that feeds on refuse or salvages waste is a scavenger.

clue.text: Urgent information needed in departure

indicators.note: needed in tells us one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: an exit is a departure
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Pressing details are required at the departure gate.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN, short for general information, is British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pressing and demanding immediate attention is urgent, a close synonym.

clue.text: European girl, say, at meeting to give explanation

indicators.note: say signals the word is wanted by its sound

parts.note: Lucy is a girl's name
a date is a meeting

explanation.surface: A European girl explains her meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: LUCI is spelt as Lucy sounds; 'at' links.
explanation.definitionFit: To make clear, to throw light on, is to elucidate.

clue.text: The lift one gets when immersed in the drink?

definitions.text: The lift one gets when immersed in the drink?

parts.words: The lift one gets when immersed in the drink?
parts.note: the 'lift' sounds like a boost from alcohol, but the drink is the sea and the lift is buoyancy

explanation.definitionFit: Archimedes' principle names the upward buoyant force on something submerged in a fluid.

clue.text: Financial return to retaliate against

definitions.meaning: the profit or recovery from an investment
as two words, to get even with someone

explanation.definitionFit: As one word it is the return on an outlay; as a phrasal verb it means taking revenge on someone.

clue.text: Excresence in trunk turning up wher taking time

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Excresence in trunk turning up wher taking time', is garbled: 'trunk turning up' hides KNUR reversed, but 'wher taking time' has no part to play and no scan or search gives the true text.
annotationWithheld.clue: Excresence in trunk turning up wher taking time

clue.text: Unconventional words on leaving

definitions.meaning: hyphenated slang for strange or avant-garde
the sign above an exit door

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain exit signs often read this phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: It is slang for weird and also the British sign marking an exit.

clue.text: The power of the inventors years

parts.note: James Watt, Scottish inventor who improved the steam engine
an age is a long period of years

explanation.surface: The power of an inventor's years of work.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed 'inventors' stands for 'inventor's'; 'The', 'of the' link.
explanation.definitionFit: Power measured in watts, an electrical rating, is this.

clue.text: Dealt with fire signal mainly in South Dakota

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside another
mainly means most of the word, its last letter lost

parts.note: a token is a sign or signal

explanation.surface: A fire signal in South Dakota was attended to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dealt with fire' looks like firefighting but means feeding a fire; 'mainly' cuts the signal word short before 'in' places it within the state's abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To feed a furnace with fuel is to tend it, attending to the fire.

clue.text: Search around the river to seek accommodation

indicators.note: around tells us one word wraps about another

parts.note: the stutter on the word mimics a stammered search, so the synonym hunt is given with its first letter doubled
the Ouse is a river in England, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: Searching along a riverbank for a place to live.
explanation.walkthrough: The stammer in 'S-search' is the device: the synonym is stammered too, and 'around' wraps it about the river after its doubled opening letter. The Ouse flows through York.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyphenated, it means looking for a home to buy or rent.

clue.text: He could be associated with pop

definitions.text: He could be associated with pop

parts.words: He could be associated with pop
parts.note: pop seems to mean father, making this a relative, but pop is also slang for pawn and this relative is slang for a pawnbroker

explanation.definitionFit: In old slang a pawnbroker is called by this family title, and to pop goods is to pawn them.

clue.text: Dress in gear change?

definitions.meaning: moving the gear lever is ... gear

explanation.definitionFit: A loose straight frock has this name, and changing gear is a move of the stick.

clue.text: Defame character on the slide?

definitions.meaning: a specimen spread on a microscope slide

explanation.definitionFit: It is a slur on someone's name and also a sample spread on a microscope glass.

clue.text: Gun ace having been in stir set free

indicators.note: in stir suggests the letters are stirred up, so they are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A top gunman was in prison and has now been released.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stir' is slang for prison, but here 'in stir' mixes GUN and ACE.
explanation.definitionFit: To release from a cage is to let something go free.

clue.text: Dance to strut at Dundee, for example

parts.note: a Dundee cake is a Scottish fruit cake topped with almonds
to strut is to walk proudly

explanation.surface: Dancing and swaggering about in a Scottish city.
explanation.walkthrough: Dundee is a Scottish city, but here it is a fruit cake named after it.
explanation.definitionFit: The cakewalk was a strutting dance from the American South, its prize originally a cake.

clue.text: Plan attempt to involve repair of hoe

indicators.note: to involve means one piece wraps another

parts.note: a try is an attempt

indicators.note: a repair of the word fixes its letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Planning to try fixing a garden tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plan' is a noun here, as in a theory of how something works; 'repair of' jumbles the tool's letters and 'to involve' wraps the attempt round them.
explanation.definitionFit: A scheme or hypothesis can be called a plan or proposition.

clue.text: Frayed end fibre (cotton)

definitions.note: to cotton on to someone is to take to them; the verb alone means become friendly

indicators.note: frayed means unravelled, so the letters come loose and rearrange

explanation.surface: A ragged end of cotton thread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frayed' rearranges END FIBRE; 'cotton', posing as the fibre, is the verb meaning to take a liking.
explanation.definitionFit: To cotton, in older use, is to get on well with someone, to make friends.
